newsitem.title: CHINA: More China policemen killed in line of duty.
newsitem.headline: More China policemen killed in line of duty.

text.p: An increasing number of Chinese police have been killed in the line of duty in recent years, and authorities have drafted rules on pensions for their bereaved families, local media said on Thursday.
The number of police officers killed in the line of duty was expected to soar to more than 400 in 1996, the China News Service said.
A total of 395 officers were killed on duty in 1995, an average of 1.08 a day, the agency said, adding that more than 8,500 policemen were injured.
Rules on pensions for police killed or wounded in the line of duty were promulgated on November 19, it said.
It did not say how much compensation families of dead police officers would receive, but said the amount would be similar to that given to families of military officers killed while on duty.

A total of 2,900 policemen were killed between 1981 and 1995, an average of 193.3 a year, the China Daily quoted Xu Jichang, vice-director of the political department under the Ministry of Public Security, as saying.
Crime, virtually eliminated in the years after the communists came to power in 1949, has staged a comeback in the past two decades along with economic reforms.
Illegal possession of firearms and gun-running are widespread in China. The crime rate has soared, prompting China to launch a highly publicised crackdown on crime in April.
